title: Discovery: Vanguard Labs - migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Initial migration discovery. Vanguard currently uses OpenAI via hosted API for prod chat + embeddings; evaluating Redwood Dedicated for cost predictability, VPC/private deployment, and parity with OpenAI outputs. Discussed throughput needs, latency targets, KV cache/prefix caching, eval parity, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS, audit logs). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share Dedicated pricing, SOC2 and private deployment docs; SE to run a short benchmark using Vanguard prompts and report latency/cost estimates; Vanguard to share traffic profile and sample prompt sets.
next_steps: Lena to send Dedicated pricing sheet and options (reserved pool vs burst) - due 2026-03-06

transcript: Meeting header: 2026-03-04, 16:00 - 16:44 PST | Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Head of ML, Vanguard Labs), Ethan Cole (Platform Engineer), Priya Shah (Security & Compliance)
00:00 Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood — happy to kick off. Marco's our SE, he'll jump into the technicals. How's everyone doing?

00:07 Sofia: Hi Lena, thanks. Doing well. We wanted to talk through options for moving off our current OpenAI hosted usage — looking at Dedicated or private options — cost, parity, and security are top of mind.

00:18 Marco: Great. Quick agenda — understand your workload and constraints, talk about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, discuss migrations and eval parity, then next steps. Sofia, could you give a quick overview of your stack?

00:29 Sofia: Sure. We run a customer support assistant and an embeddings index for semantic search. Currently prod on OpenAI GPT-4o-ish endpoints via hosted API; embeddings with text-embedding-ada-002-ish. Traffic pattern is bursty — peak around 120 qps for chat, avg token lengths around 350, 95th around 900 for longer threads. Cost is scaling fast so ops asked us to explore Dedicated. Also, we have internal requirements for audit logs and optional VPC for some enterprise customers.
00:58 Ethan: On infra side we use k8s in Azure, and we already have service accounts and SSO. We need predictable per-token spend — the openai bills keep spiking and makes budgeting difficult.

01:09 Lena: Understood. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives control for data residency. Marco, can you explain how parity works — folks often ask about output differences when switching providers or runtimes like vLLM/TGI.

01:25 Marco: Yeah, so short version: model compatibility and prompt engineering matter. If you're using OpenAI models, Redwood can host tuned open-source equivalents, but you'll see drift. We focus on eval parity through two approaches: 1) replicate prompt conditioning and sampling params exactly, 2) run A/B evals and adjust temperature/hyperparams or finetune if needed. Also note differences with runtimes — e.g., vLLM or TGI may have subtle tokenization or sampling differences, and KV cache semantics can change latency profiles — sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in notes — but it's basically the same component, prefix/KV caching to speed up repeated context.
02:12 Priya: For us security is make-or-break. SOC2 or ISO reports, encryption at rest with KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. How does Redwood Dedicated handle keys and auditability?

02:24 Marco: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration and we emit audit logs for request-level events. Private deployments let you keep control of the network. We also have RBAC and SAML SSO integrations on the console. We'll share SOC2 docs after call.
02:40 Sofia: Nice. On quality — we can't accept regressions on intent extraction. We run a continuous eval suite tied to PRs. How do you prevent model drift when moving to hosted Open weights?

02:52 Marco: We recommend running your eval suite against candidate model variants on Redwood first. We'll run parallel inference on a small holdout set to measure metric drift. If drift exists, options are parameter tuning, prompt engineering, or hosting a finetuned variant. Also caching and batching changes don't affect quality, just latency/cost tradeoffs.
03:18 Ethan: Quick question about throughput: our 120 qps peak is mostly short requests, but we have long chat sessions too. What's typical latency on Dedicated for GPT-like models?

03:30 Marco: Depends on model size and quantization. For a 13B quantized runtime we often see 90th percentile latencies under 300ms for single-turn short prompts with optimized kernels and batching; long context chats increase latencies due to KV ops. We can tune batching to balance cost vs tail latency. We'll need your token distribution to model costs accurately.
03:58 Sofia: We're using a lot of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — embeddings calls are frequent. Any differences in embedding quality or formats?

04:10 Marco: We can host popular embedding models locally; output vectors are usually compatible but you should validate downstream similarity scores. There can be small variations in tokenizer or normalization. We'll run your embedding set through our model candidates as part of the benchmark.

04:28 Lena: On migration plan — typical path: 1) run a pilot on Dedicated (small reserved pool), 2) benchmark with your prompts, 3) validate eval suite, 4) plan cutover and rollbacks. Questions so far?
04:37 Priya: On compliance — for customers in EU, data residency matters. Does Redwood allow region pinning and audit retention configs?
04:46 Marco: Yes, Dedicated and Private support region pinning and configurable audit retention. For Private on-prem you control retention fully. We'll include those options in the docs.
05:00 Sofia: Regarding sample size for benchmarks — what do you need from us?

05:06 Marco: Ideally 50-100 representative prompts for chat; sample embedding queries (500) for vector tests; traffic pattern including p50/p95 token lengths and qps. Also success criteria — latency SLO and acceptable quality delta on your eval metrics.
05:22 Ethan: Do you support a canary rollout or A/B testing on Redwood Dedicated? We want gradual cutovers.

05:29 Lena: Yes — rollouts and canaries are supported. You can route a percentage of traffic to Dedicated variants, or do shadow testing. The Console provides per-route performance and cost breakdowns.
05:40 Sofia: A couple of gotchas we've heard — vLLM speeds up throughput, but we've read reports of non-deterministic sampling in some runtimes. Any notes?

05:52 Marco: That's right — runtime differences can affect decoding at the tail. We recommend identical sampling seeds when possible, and run paired comparisons. If determinism is critical, you might need to pin runtime+model version and avoid certain async batching modes that reorder tokens — Redwood can configure that.
06:14 Priya: On contracts — how long are Dedicated commitments? And what about overage/burst behavior?
06:22 Lena: Typical reserved commitments are monthly or annual; burst capacity is an option for handling spikes. Pricing sheet I'll send will detail reserved vs burst rates and cutover terms.
06:33 Sofia: Can you give us a rough back-of-envelope cost compare vs OpenAI for our workload?

06:39 Marco: We can but it depends on batch sizes and caching efficiency. With prefix caching and batching, it's common for customers to see 20-50% lower per-token costs versus hosted OpenAI for large sustained workloads. We'll run your actual profile through our estimator for accuracy.
07:00 Ethan: Integration-wise, how do we route traffic? Do you offer a drop-in API or do we need client changes?

07:08 Marco: Redwood API aims to be compatible but not a byte-for-byte drop-in. We provide SDKs and REST endpoints; many customers implement a small adapter layer. For embeddings and chat semantics, you'll likely only need minor changes in param names. We'll provide migration notes.
07:25 Lena: Let's talk about timelines — when would you be able to provide prompts and traffic?
07:29 Sofia: We can collect and share by next Monday (2026-03-09).
07:33 Lena: Great. Marco will run benchmarks once you share. We'll target a follow-up in two weeks for results and infra deep-dive.

07:41 Marco: One more technical nit: if you're using GPUs on Azure and self-hosting, note that I/O of large KV caches can be network heavy. Dedicated reduces that by colocating serving. We'll include model/quantization recommendations.
07:58 Sofia: For embeddings, we care about 99th percentile latency for retrieval — we can't add a 2s tail. Does Redwood provide per-token traces?
08:07 Marco: Yes. The Console offers per-route traces and token-level cost/latency breakdowns. We can set up alerts for 95/99th breaches.
08:20 Priya: A question on logs: Are payloads redacted in audit logs? We need to ensure PII isn't stored in plain text.
08:29 Marco: We support redaction rules and can exclude or hash payloads in logs. For Private deployments, you can also keep logs inside your VPC.
08:38 Sofia: Any known incompatibilities when migrating from OpenAI endpoints to open-source models hosted on Redwood? For example some prompts that relied on system-level instructions?

08:49 Marco: System prompts can behave differently across models. We recommend capturing system messages and running them through the candidate model; sometimes you need to rephrase. We'll run that as part of the eval. Also watch out for tokenization differences affecting contextual length accounting.
09:05 Ethan: If we decide to keep some traffic on OpenAI and some on Redwood, can we do hybrid routing by policy?
09:11 Lena: Yes — smart routing policies based on latency, cost, region, or customer-tier are supported; automatic fallback to a compatible variant is also configurable.
09:21 Sofia: Sounds promising. Any blockers from Redwood side for starting a pilot?
09:26 Marco: No blockers — we'll need the prompts, sample payloads, and an account setup for pilot. We can use a small reserved pool to simulate steady state and use burst for spikes.
09:35 Lena: Okay, let's recap next steps quickly — I'll send pricing and SOC2/PII docs; Marco will prepare benchmark plan; Sofia will share prompts and traffic. Any other asks?
09:46 Priya: Please include SAML metadata and sample security questionnaire answers in the packet.
09:51 Marco: Will do. We'll also include a short how-to for running the eval suite against candidate models.
09:58 Sofia: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark results.
10:02 Lena: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the packet by Friday. Bye!

11:00 Post-call notes: Lena uploaded Dedicated pricing link and SOC2; Marco started drafting benchmark plan. Customer to share prompts by target date. Transcription contains occasional mishears (vLLM as V L L M, KV cache as KV cash).
